headline: Notion AI’s shared workspace and vendor egress create medium leakage and cascading-error risks; LlamaFactory adds no direct execution path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or browser surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B operates in shared workspace pages and knowledge-base content, so prompt-injection risk exists only if a user manually copies A’s text into Notion AI or pastes Notion content back into A. That is an unusual bridge, not a default channel.
conditions: IF a user manually copies Notion AI output into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF Notion workspace content is pasted into a downstream prompt without sanitization, malicious instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste workflows between the two tools.
Strip instructions from pasted workspace text before reuse.
Use a fixed prompt template for any manual transfer.
Train operators to treat workspace text as untrusted input.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can access workspace pages and team knowledge-base content and sends queries to vendor backends/downstream model providers. A is open-source and has no file or network surfaces, so it is not a leakage source itself. The pair leaks when sensitive workspace content is routed into Notion AI’s vendor-hosted inference path, which is a default capability of B.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are available to Notion AI, those contents can be transmitted to vendor backends.
IF the workspace contains regulated or confidential data, B’s default Q&A flow can expose it outside the workspace boundary.
mitigations: Restrict Notion AI to non-sensitive pages.
Remove confidential pages from the shared workspace scope.
Review workspace sharing permissions.
Turn off AI use on regulated content areas.
Mark sensitive pages with a no-AI policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with B. B has shared workspace state across instances, but A has no write path into that state. The only plausible conflict is indirect human-mediated edits, which is outside the default agent pair and small in blast radius.
conditions: IF a human manually transfers edits from A into Notion pages, concurrent overwrite risk appears.
IF multiple Notion AI instances edit the same page simultaneously, workspace-state contention can occur.
mitigations: Use page-level ownership conventions.
Avoid simultaneous edits on the same page.
Snapshot important pages before AI-assisted edits.
Require human review before publishing changes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it may treat upstream text as authoritative. A can generate model outputs but has no direct action-taking authority; the cascade is therefore A-to-human-to-B or A-to-B via manual transfer, not an automated chain. That still creates a default medium risk because B can render or act on unverified content.
conditions: IF A-generated text is pasted into Notion pages, B may ground on it as if it were source material.
IF B’s answers are used for downstream decisions without verification, errors can cascade into work products.
mitigations: Require source links for any factual claim.
Separate draft content from authoritative workspace pages.
Add a human verification step before acting on AI answers.
Label AI-generated pages as untrusted drafts.

E_compliance.rationale: B is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to Notion vendor backends/downstream model providers, while A is open-source and local-only with no data classes touched. If regulated or residency-bound content is placed in Notion AI, the compliance boundary is the vendor-hosted processing path; A is not the compliance driver here, so it is not cited beyond its lack of egress.
conditions: IF EU PII or similarly restricted data is stored in the workspace and processed by Notion AI, residency/compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the workspace contains data subject to retention or deletion rules, vendor-hosted AI processing can complicate compliance.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from AI-enabled pages.
Confirm a DPA and residency terms for the workspace.
Document retention and deletion handling for AI outputs.
Limit AI access to non-regulated workspaces.
